newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: OCBC INTERIM PROFITS SURPRISE ANALYSTS.
newsitem.headline: OCBC INTERIM PROFITS SURPRISE ANALYSTS.

text.p: Singapore's Overseas-Chinese Banking Corporation Ltd (OCBC) surprised analysts on Friday with better than expected profits for six months ended June 30, 1997.
The group announced a 11.3 percent rise in interim net profits to Singapore $339.09 million. At bank level, profits grew 62.3 percent to S$217.84 million.
Analysts said they were expecting the group's interim profits to grow 11 to 13 percent, but if the sharp drop in other income was discounted, growth was much higher than the expected range.

"This set of results, while you can't jump for joy, is reasonable considering the fact they came off strongly on the other income side," investment analyst Sim Shyh Yang at Keppel Securities Pte Ltd told Reuters.
The group's other income fell to S$79.68 million from S$125.63 million in the first six months of 1997.
The analysts said they were unfazed by this 36.6 percent drop as it was against a high base last year when the grou booked profits from property developments.
"The fall in other income is not a sign of recurring weakness in the core banking operations. As long as the core is still strong, it will be all right," an analyst at JM Sassoon said.
Continued strength in the group's core operations was reflected in the 24.4 percent rise in the bank's interest income to S$1.02 billion and a 21.6 percent rise to S$1.64 billion at the group level.
These, analysts said, were stronger than those recently announced by United Overseas Bank and DBS Bank.
"It means loans growth is good, either in the mid to the high teens," said the JM Sassoon analyst.

Analysts were mostly optimistic about the group's 1997 earnings and said they expected good rental contributions from the new office complexes. Profits from other property developments were expected to fuel 1998 earnings.
According to the Edinburgh Financial Publishing's Estimate directory, the group's 1997 earnings are forecast at S$810.1 million.
